THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Wight, J. Ambrose | Letter. | October 28, 1843. Ordained | to Miniitry” (second_presb_0914, printed page 205), admitted 1843-10-28 by letter. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Wight' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins J. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

merge_ruling.for_merge: A dropped r, and the initial J agrees with 'J. Wright' of the American of 11 July 1835 (#c004).
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE INITIAL J HAS TWO RIVALS AMONG THE WRIGHTS AND THE `wright` CLUSTER HAS ALREADY SAID SO. Its standing U1/R2 ruling refuses a bare 'J. Wright' because the father and the son share the forename John and the initial cannot choose between them; folding the surname as well adds a third candidate and removes nothing. 'J. F. Wight' is one reading, the Democrat of 11 June 1834 (#c007), and its middle initial F is carried by no Wright of this town — John S. Wright's is S, and T-0997's C2 merge inside that cluster turned on exactly that printed letter. The town holds six Wright cards and one Wight. Refused by a ratified rule; no ballot needed.
